items.author: Jake Johnson
items.title: 21 Senate Democrats Join GOP to End Debate on Big Oil-Backed ‘Kill Switch for Future Climate Action’
items.summary: Common Dreams reports that 21 Democrats joined Republicans in the 70-27 cloture vote, with Cortez Masto the one Democrat who flipped to no, and quotes Oil Change International's Elizabeth Bast calling the bill a kill switch for future climate action.

quote.text: BAAJA would act as a kill switch for future climate action without offering any meaningful emissions reductions
quote.speaker: Elizabeth Bast, executive director, Oil Change International

items.title: Re: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (S. 5653 / H.R. 2347): Twelve Provisions That Should Not Become Law
items.summary: Environmental and energy law scholars write to Senate Democratic leaders that BAAJA would damage NEPA, the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act; the letter is dated November 13 and was updated with more signatures on November 16.

quote.text: would inflict permanent, sweeping damage on the nation's core environmental laws
quote.speaker: Environmental and energy law scholars (letter signatories)

items.title: New Mexico US Sen. Heinrich’s permitting bill takes another step toward US Senate passage
items.summary: Source NM reports the Senate voted 70-27 to end debate on the substitute Heinrich co-wrote, that Sen. Luján voted no, and that Al Gore and Pueblo governors urged senators to wait or reject it.

quote.text: The vote clears the way for the U.S. Senate to take a final vote on the bill as early as this week.
quote.speaker: Source New Mexico (reporting)

items.title: Stage set for vote this week on permitting reform Act
items.summary: Oklahoma Energy Today reports Sens. Lankford and Armstrong voted for cloture and quotes Armstrong urging passage on the Senate floor.

quote.text: After ten years of endless debate, we finally have industry, labor, and a broad bipartisan coalition aligned
quote.speaker: Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-Okla.)

items.title: Senate Advances Permitting Bill 70-27 As Jeffries Opposes It
items.summary: HNGN reports the 70-27 cloture vote on the substitute, House Democratic leader Jeffries saying the bill falls short, and analysts putting lame-duck passage odds at 20 to 25 percent.

quote.text: The vote cleared the 60-vote threshold with room to spare, but the bill has a harder path in the House.
quote.speaker: HNGN (reporting)

items.author: Jeff St. John
items.title: Permitting reform is a big, controversial bet for the energy transition
items.summary: Canary Media's chief reporter lays out the bill as a three-part bet by Democrats and clean energy advocates, and notes the Senate voted 70-27 Monday to end debate.

quote.text: The Senate bipartisan permitting bill is essentially an enormous three-part bet by the Democrats and clean energy advocates who support it.
quote.speaker: Jeff St. John, Canary Media

items.author: Sarah Liese (Twilla)
items.title: Senate expected to vote on permitting bill tribal leaders in Oklahoma, beyond oppose
items.summary: KOSU reports tribal nations and preservation groups ask senators to reject the bill, quotes NCAI President Mark Macarro, and notes the Crow Tribe has expressed approval.

quote.text: Any amendment to S. 5653 merely puts lipstick on a pig
quote.speaker: Mark Macarro, President, NCAI

items.title: Congress returns to work with Indian Country on the agenda — and on the menu
items.summary: KBFT's Indian Country roundup reports the 70-27 cloture vote cleared a path for final passage before Thanksgiving, over what it calls widespread opposition in Indian Country.

quote.text: the Senate has cleared a path for final passage of BAAJA in H.R.2347 before the Thanksgiving break
quote.speaker: KBFT (reporting)

items.author: Oliver Milman
items.title: Passing bill to speed up gas projects and datacenters would be ‘serious mistake’, Al Gore says
items.summary: The Guardian reports former Vice President Al Gore, at the COP31 summit in Antalya, called passing the bill a serious mistake given the midterm results.

quote.text: I think it would be a serious mistake, particularly in the wake of the astonishing election results last week
quote.speaker: Al Gore, former Vice President

items.outlet: Congressional Record, Senate, Nov 16, 2026 (Energy, pp. S5676-S5678)
items.author: Sen. Edward Markey (D-Mass.)
items.title: Energy
items.summary: Sen. Markey says on the Senate floor that the permitting bill is sold as an affordability fix but makes it harder for communities to challenge projects, and raises data centers on public lands.

quote.text: Part of how this bill makes it easier to do all of those things is by making it harder for you, for your community, to do anything about it, now or forever.
quote.speaker: Sen. Edward Markey (D-Mass.)

items.author: Emily Pontecorvo
items.title: How Tribal Rights Became Central to the Permitting Debate
items.summary: Heatmap reports nearly 30 Democrats back a Schiff amendment to strike the historic preservation section, that Murkowski and Schatz filed a narrower fix, and that Padilla and western Democrats proposed exempting tribal claims from the judicial review limit.

quote.text: The amendment filed by Senators Murkowski and Schatz on Tuesday would make one small change, ensuring that all projects that receive federal funding go through NHPA reviews instead of just those that also require some form of federal approval.
quote.speaker: Emily Pontecorvo, Heatmap News

amendment_count.quote: SA 7022. Mr. LEE (for himself, Mr. Heinrich, Mrs. Capito, and Mr. Whitehouse) submitted an amendment intended to be proposed to amendment SA 6883
amendment_count.method: Counted from the Congressional Record 'Text of Amendments' headers on govinfo (Nov 10 to Nov 17, SA 6849 to SA 7023): 128 headed 'to amendment SA 6883' (125 filed through Nov 16, 3 on Nov 17), plus 44 headed 'to the bill H.R. 2347'. Congress.gov (blocked, 403 via r.jina.ai) showed 113 as of Nov 16 in the site's existing data; the two counts differ and congress.gov could not be read to reconcile them. SA 6884 and 6885 are Thune amendments to SA 6883 and are inside the 128.

point_of_order.what_source_says: The Record and the Press Gallery name a Merkley point of order against substitute amendment No. 6883 and set the vote for 11:45 a.m. on Nov 18, but give no Budget Act section or claim. No news or official source read says which section or what it asserts.

sources.publisher: Congressional Record, Senate, Nov 17, 2026 (Orders for Wednesday)
sources.quote: if Senator Merkley or his designee raises a point of order on substitute amendment No. 6883, the Senate vote in relation to the point of order at 11:45 a.m.
